title: Memory leak essence
key_conclusions: Android memory leaks are lifecycle mismatch plus strong reachability from a GC Root, not a collector failure.
GC can only reclaim unreachable objects; if a retained path still exists, manual GC or collector tuning cannot fix the root cause.
A leak investigation should identify the Root, owner, bridge, victim, and first incorrect ownership edge with heap dump evidence.
When GC freed bytes stay low, the next engineering step is retained-path analysis plus memory-category attribution, not more GC speculation.
